speaker: Doctor
text: Hello, I am Dr. Agent. To begin assessing your knee swelling, can you tell me when the symptoms first started and if you experienced any specific injury or trauma prior to the onset?

speaker: Patient
text: 18-month-old boy. The patient is brought in by his parents due to swelling in his right knee noticed after playing in the park. The parents report that there was no obvious injury or incident at the park that could have led to the swelling. Upon further questioning, the mother recalls that an uncle on her side of the family had similar problems, suggesting a possible genetic component.

speaker: Doctor
text: Does the swelling come and go on its own, and have you noticed any episodes of unusually long bleeding times after minor cuts or vaccinations? Also, does the child have any joint pain when the knee is not swollen?

speaker: Patient
text: My main symptom is Swelling of the right knee. I also have No recent trauma or injury, Familial history of similar symptoms.

speaker: Doctor
text: Does the child have a history of excessive bruising or prolonged bleeding from minor cuts, and has he experienced swelling in other joints like elbows or ankles? I would also like to check his coagulation profile to rule out a bleeding disorder. REQUEST TEST: Coagulation_Panel

speaker: Measurement
text: RESULTS: ACT: 52.0 s (prolonged), PT: 14.0 s, Thrombin time: < 2 seconds deviation from control.

speaker: Doctor
text: The prolonged Activated Clotting Time (ACT) with a normal Prothrombin Time (PT) strongly suggests a deficiency in the intrinsic coagulation pathway, likely Hemophilia A or B. REQUEST TEST: Factor_VIII_and_Factor_IX_assay

speaker: Doctor
text: The normal factor levels are unexpected given the prolonged ACT, so I need to check for an inhibitor or other specific coagulopathy. REQUEST TEST: Factor_VIII_inhibitor_titer

speaker: Doctor
text: Given the normal factor levels and inhibitor titer, I suspect a different bleeding disorder like von Willebrand disease. Let's check the specific platelet function. REQUEST TEST: Von_Willebrand_Factor_Antigen

speaker: Doctor
text: With coagulation studies and von Willebrand factor normal, I must consider non-hemorrhagic causes like juvenile idiopathic arthritis or infection. REQUEST TEST: Joint_Aspiration_and_Culture

speaker: Measurement
text: RESULTS: Joint aspiration reveals grossly bloody fluid (hemarthrosis). Gram stain and culture are negative for bacterial infection.

speaker: Doctor
text: The presence of hemarthrosis with negative cultures and normal standard coagulation factors strongly suggests a rare bleeding disorder or a specific factor deficiency not yet tested. Given the family history and the isolated prolonged ACT, I suspect Hemophilia C (Factor XI deficiency), which can present with normal PT and variable aPTT/ACT depending on the assay. DIAGNOSIS READY: Hemophilia C (Factor XI Deficiency)
